original_record.subject: accounts
original_record.question: What is the cardinal rule of the double entry system?

options.A: Debit the increasing account and credit the decreasing account.
options.B: Debit the receiving account and credit the giving account.
options.C: Debit the asset account and credit the liability account.
options.D: Debit the revenue account and credit the expenditure account.

original_record.ai_explanation: The cardinal rule of double entry bookkeeping is to debit the receiving account and credit the giving account for every transaction.

records.hold_reason: Debit the receiver and credit the giver is a traditional real-account mnemonic, not a universal cardinal rule for every account. None states the universal equal-debit-and-credit principle accurately.

original_record.question: The discount column of a three column cashbook is not balanced off but periodically transferred to the discount accounts because discounts.

options.C: do not form part of double entry

original_record.ai_explanation: Discount columns are not balanced off but transferred periodically to discount accounts because discounts do not form part of the double entry bookkeeping process in the cashbook.
